title: Released Windows updater locks its own console launcher
signatures: failed to remove file[^\r\n]*Scripts[/\\]slave\.exe[^\r\n]*Access is denied\. \(os error 5\)
explanation: The March/April Windows updater is already running from slave.exe when uv tries to replace it. Windows refuses the locked launcher. The update target cannot change that loaded code; re-running the installer is a separate recovery route.

title: July script installs offer a manual update instead of an app hand-off
errors: ^E2E ASSERTION FAILED: app driven via captured slave desktop spec; update completed$
^E2E ASSERTION FAILED: GUI driver clicked Update now and the app quit for hand-off$
signatures: \[updates\] no staged updater; surfacing manual `slave update` for CLI install at
explanation: The July Windows app has no staged updater after a script install. Its Update button explicitly returns manual: slave update without starting a hand-off. Desktop-installer installs are not covered by this exception.

title: June Slave-Setup.dmg updater is refused by the v2026.7.30 update lock
errors: ^E2E ASSERTION FAILED: app-driven update exited 1; transcript above$
signatures: bootstrap\.log: ✗ Another slave-agent update is already running \(PID [0-9]+, started [^\r\n]* stage=update
slave_bootstrap_lib::update: update stage stage=update state=Failed [^\r\n]*slave-agent is still running\. Close all slave-agent windows and try the update again\.
explanation: The published June Slave-Setup.dmg updater writes the update marker with its own PID, then runs the v2026.7.30 checkout's slave update. That release recognises its orchestrator only through SLAVE_UPDATE_HANDOFF_PID, which the June binary predates, so the pre-pull CLI refuses with Another slave-agent update is already running. The update target cannot change that loaded code; slave update from a terminal or re-running the installer recovers.
